pr_title: Create custom Trim parameter class and overload the trim methods
pr_body:
Fixes #3803 

Deprecate the existing XTRIM methods available in any interface where the TrimStrategy is supported, and overload with one
that accepts a generic TrimParam.

This allows to pass in different types than the current `int` values, to support the full semantics of MINID.

Such TrimParam can only be created via smart constructors, to improve on type safety and user ergonomics.

issue_context.title: Redis Stream XTRIM with MINID strategy is not fully supported: incompatible parameter type
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
The API to trim a redis stream ([see the correspoding XTRIM command](https://redis.io/commands/xtrim)) supports different strategies via the [org.redisson.api.stream.TrimStrategy](https://javadoc.io/doc/org.redisson/redisson/latest/org/redisson/api/stream/TrimStrategy.html) type.
Yet the additional command parameters in the overloaded methods (e.g. trim, trimAsync, trimNonStrictAsync) will allow only `int`s.
Specifically you can now only pass a
* `int threshold` (to say how many messages you want to keep)
* `int limit` (to remove up to a given number of messages)

Those are inconsistent with the `TrimStrategy.MINID` which expects a message Id as input.

Since the message Ids are composed of a timestamp in millis from epoch and a number, the current `int` param won't be able to technically be used for such a job, even ignoring the semantics of the param.
An `int` is not enough to encode a valid millis timestamp which is part of the message Id.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
It would be nice to provide overloaded methods taking an instance of [org.redisson.api.StreamMessageId](https://github.com/redisson/redisson/blob/master/redisson/src/main/java/org/redisson/api/StreamMessageId.java), and - most importantly- a simple `String`, to allow partial matches.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I will probably use a work-around by calling the low-level redis client, but the issue is mostly about the current API which is a bit misleading in what it provides.
